learning_objective: 🎯 You will learn how to count nouns as singular or plural and classify them into four different genders easily!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A noun that stands for only one person or thing is Singular. When it stands for more than one, it is Plural! We often make plurals by adding -s or -es, like changing 'box' to 'boxes'.
Nouns that refer to males (boys, men, male animals) belong to the Masculine gender. Nouns that refer to females (girls, women, female animals) belong to the Feminine gender, like 'king' and 'queen'.
Some words can be used for both males and females! These belong to the Common gender. Words like 'doctor', 'teacher', or 'friend' do not tell us if the person is a boy or a girl.
Non-living things have no gender! Words for things without life, like 'book', 'table', or 'pencil', are placed in the Neuter gender category.

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Family Tree Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Write down the names of 5 family members and label their gender, then find 3 singular items in your school bag and write their plural forms!

quick_recap: ⭐ Singular means one, and Plural means more than one.
⭐ Masculine nouns are for males, and Feminine nouns are for females.
⭐ Common gender nouns can be either male or female, while Neuter gender nouns are for non-living things.
